final_lessons: Under very tight step budgets, higher effective learning rates tend to dominate performance more than architectural capacity.
Very low learning rates (~0.0001) are consistently underpowered for short budgets, and Adam tends to outperform RMSprop at comparable settings.
Larger d_model=128 architectures with moderate-lr adaptive optimizers (Adam/AdamW ~0.0003) have been consistently strong on this dataset.
Adam at lr=0.003 tends to underperform, so prefer optimizers whose effective lr decays (Adagrad) or moderate lrs when only high-lr options remain.
The d_model=128 plus Adam/AdamW at lr~0.0003 combination remains the reliable winner on this bigram dataset.
When the strong d_model=128 architecture is absent, favor AdamW with a moderate learning rate over RMSprop or low-lr SGD.
The d_model=128, 3-layer, AdamW lr=0.0003 configuration is a dominant setup that consistently achieves the best test loss on this dataset.
Adaptive optimizers (Adam/AdamW) at lr~0.0003 consistently beat plain SGD at low learning rates on this dataset.
d_model=128 combined with any adaptive optimizer at moderate lr remains the strongest available choice, outperforming small models and low-lr SGD.
The large d_model=128 architecture with a moderate-lr adaptive optimizer remains the safest winning bet, avoiding both excessively high (0.01) and excessively low (0.0001) learning rates.
